input.objective: Launch PLEA test run 3 on Sepolia from this Foundry repository exactly as launch.json lists it: five contracts (PLEA, CabalGate, Seasons, PleaDistributor, PleaLaunch), deployed in order in one transaction with the constructor arguments in launch.json. This is the code of launch #1311 (your accepted run-2 adaptation and its audit fixes kept) plus the changes below. (1) Letters and auto-sell: a new ownerless Letterbox, deployed after the launch by anyone through PleaLaunch.deployLetterbox(creationCode), which checks the code against the keccak256 committed in launch.json, deploys it with CREATE2 (the Letterbox takes no constructor arguments and reads its settings from PleaLaunch) and registers it once with PLEA.setLetterbox; like the hook it is not a launch.json entry. Anyone pleads by sending a transaction whose input data is the plea text (fallback), or by calling letter(text) with the same text from a block explorer's Write Contract tab; commands APPEAL, SELL and NAME (a command word alone is the command, never a plea; an APPEAL letter may retry an appeal the oracle never answered); a letter pleads a fixed 20% of the writer's PLEA, held in escrow. The oracle fee, a 0.25 IMD runner tip and an appeal's 0.35 IMD wall share are paid in the same transaction by the gate selling the writer's PLEA for exactly that IMD (exact-output swap through the hook, at most the hourly snapshot value plus 10%; on Sepolia the Letterbox mints the 0.5 test oracle fee instead, a setting refused on chain id 1). Anyone sells an approved escrowed plea with deliver for at least 95% of its snapshot value and earns the tip; the gate pays the sale's IMD to the Letterbox, which sends the 0.35 IMD auto-sell fee to Seasons (checkpointed into the running season's prize pot) and the rest to the writer, and refuses up front a plea worth less than 0.70 IMD at the snapshot; the fee is taken only from a sale, and selling by hand through the gate costs nothing extra; settle returns the escrow and the tip on every other ending; status and leaderboard are text views; display names (setName or a NAME letter: 3-20 characters a-z 0-9 _, unique) live in the Letterbox. No Letterbox function ID can be the start of valid UTF-8 text (a test checks the ABI). CabalGate gains submitFor, appealFor and executeSellFor that only the Letterbox may call, plea flags with a PleaFlags event, and lastPleaOf; its own executeSell refuses escrowed pleas. PLEA gains setLetterbox (launcher only, once) and courtTake (Letterbox only, moving the caller's own PLEA into escrow); the Letterbox is an exempt sender. (2) Laureates (the season NFTs) are removed; Seasons no longer ranks pleas or mints. (3) A plea is at least 1% of the seller's balance, or 2.5M PLEA when that is less, and at most 50% of it (was 35%); the fact score's share-of-balance bands are 18 points up to 20%, 11 up to 35%, 5 above (were 15% and 25%). (4) The PLEA owner does not play: no season points, IMD prize, PLEA bonus or rebalance keeper tip. (5) A six-season PLEA bonus: PLEA.init mints 87% to the hook, 3% to Seasons and 10% to the distributor; each of the first six seasons pays 5,000,000 PLEA to its qualifying top 10 and burns the unpaid rest; flushToWall burns what is left; nobody can withdraw it. (6) The Cabal's judging rules version 2 in CabalGate.DEFINITIONS (plea, stories, content, manipulation, answer), calibrated with live Sepolia panels: keep the text exactly. (7) A gas pass that changes no behaviour: the oracle body JSON-escapes only the plea texts, the text rules read bytes without bounds checks, PleaHook.latestPrice and price24hAgo read one checkpoint and scan the ring only as a fallback, and a Letterbox escrow fits one slot; test/GasPass.t.sol holds each to the code it replaced. The launch transaction must fit Ethereum's 16,777,216 per-transaction gas cap with the headroom your deployer adds to the gas limit: test/LaunchManifest.t.sol measures it as the chain charges it, plus your factory's overhead as measured by sending these five codes through your mainnet ProjectFactory on a fork (12.7M, 15.5M with 22% headroom), and asserts it; keep any fix within that. An independent pre-audit found three low issues, fixed here with tests (test/AuditRun3.t.sol): an APPEAL letter can retry an appeal that got no verdict, a Letterbox appeal is clamped to 50% of the current balance (appealFor takes the amount), and a bare command word is never a paid plea. Audit the imported code and deploy it unchanged; fix only what the audit proves is a real bug, and keep every number as it is (fees, timings, panel 30, quorum 17, 5-hour seasons, 33-hour dead-man, START 1792162800, credit gas 1300000, letters 20%, plea maximum 50%, share bands 20/35, tip 0.25 IMD, auto-sell fee 0.35 IMD to the season pot, 0.70 IMD minimum plea value, 95% sale minimum, fee cap +10%, 1% plea minimum, six bonus seasons of 5,000,000 PLEA, the 87/3/10 split). If you change the Letterbox, update its code hash in launch.json (a test checks it). CabalGate's runtime is 24,315 bytes, 261 under the EIP-170 limit: keep any fix within it. Keep PLEA.setLauncher accepting either the deploy-transaction flag or PLEA's deployment block. Keep foundry.toml as it is, including [lint] lint_on_build = false and the read-only fs_permissions for ./out and ./launch.json. test/LetterboxInvariant.t.sol checks the Letterbox's custody under random letters, verdicts, deliveries and settles in both fee modes, and test/fork/ForkMainnet.t.sol (with MAINNET_RPC_URL) rehearses letters against the real IMD, sIMD, PoolManager and Intake v2 on an Ethereum fork.
